Hyatt’s concierge service for globalists is generally useless.

So while having to choose concierge service over other benefits is a devaluation of globalist service, it’s, practically speaking, not a huge loss for most members.

The loss of free parking on award-redemption stays is somewhat similar. On paper, it’s a significant devaluation. However, how many guests actually use it? If I’m going a resort, I’m not arriving with a car. Same for if I’m redeeming points to stay at the Park Hyatt in Paris or wherever. So, practically speaking, it may not be a huge loss for many elites.

What I don’t understand is why wouldn’t you come up with better offerings for globalists who do 100, 120 or 150+ nights?

I wish they would have created a benefit to compensate for the growing number of Hyatt Regency and Grand Hyatt properties WITHOUT an open or operational club lounge.

By the way, I would note that eliminating free parking on award stays is great for owners/franchisees. They can’t charge you a resort or destination fee. But now they can charge you $70 or $100 for parking that used to be free. In short, it’s a way to extract a portion of the revenue lost from waived resort or destination fees from a segment of guests who arrive with a car and want to park it at the hotel.

Outstanding article, Gary, with a lot of nuance missed by others. Don’t know if your Hyatt contacts gave you the answer to this, but if you don’t choose a Concierge at 60 nights, will you still have access to the Globalist telephone number? I have used my Concierge once or twice in the last five years, but I have used the Globalist line quite a bit.

Hi Gary. Do you know if not selecting the concierge benefit next year will still give you access to the concierge line? I can live without the MHC, but the concierge line is something I frequently use for everything.

Soooooo what if a Globalist gives another member a Guest of Honor award? Presumably the GofH will no longer be eligible to receive free parking?

@PH – GoH on its own will no longer mean free parking on award redemption, you’d have to gift both a goh + free parking award if you want them to have both but they’ll stack

Interesting. I have used the free parking benefit four times a year in New York. Andaz charges $90/nt for my suv. That’s nearly $200 for two nts The other times have been at other properties for $45-$65/nt for 6 nts@ around $300. I would say that’s a significant devaluation.

@DSK – having a concierge doesn’t preclude you from using the globalist number, but you can also just use the concierge # to speak with a concierge even if your own is not available

I think for the most part, (other than the switch from AA to DL) these are positive improvements overall. When is the last time you could say that about ANY loyalty program? Almost everything I’ve written to Hyatt about for the past two years has finally occurred…particularly the 1 yr expiration on threshold night awards. I agree with @FNT Delta Diamond that they need to enhance the rewards for power users…Perhaps for 2028 they could institute a “rollover” option for elites with 110+ nights: maybe allow excess nights above 100 to rollover to the next year’s qualifying year so that Globalist renewal is automatic or much easier? Or perhaps a single year “boost” if one doesn’t hit 60 in the next year? Just a thought. As this shows, it never hurts to ask!

Rooms for points mostly grossly overpriced. Chase transfer cut last straw. No bueno

I call BS on Hyatt saying Globalists don’t use the free parking. This actively costs them hard cash and they wanted to minimize the cash outlay.

Of course Globalists are using free parking on award stays. They are going after the travel hacking community and not the road warriors who earn Globalist on paid stays, because they weren’t getting free parking on paid stays. Easy for them to blur those lines but we can see through their statement.

https://youtube.com/shorts/WpGW1-wVv7Y?si=uSj-ikgis-9UnX4b

I feel it’s overall a downgrade, but like the fact that FNA will last longer, and the ability to stack awards is great. Also, if the online booking upgrades work the way intended, I don’t know that I will need a concierge. That’s the main thing I call for (combine an award and cash booking, and use on SNA, for example).

I see this as almost entirely a devaluation. Most of the new choices strike me as borderline thoughtless/pointless additions – the award at ten nights is basically useless for me and I’m honestly tempted to ignore it when it hits (probably by mid-January) – and whatever their bloviation may say, when the parking thing matters, it makes a big effing dent, and parking fees are showing up in more and more dubiously-justified places all the time. Losing that would be worth throwing the baby out with the bath water here, and possibly throwing the bath out as well – the “alternatives” it let them introduce aren’t worth the trade.

I realize that perspectives can legitimately vary, but this is a noticeable devaluation with a few minimal bright spots (being better able to bundle three Cat 1-7 awards is nice), but taken as a whole I’d rather tell them to shove the whole package somewhere the sun don’t shine.

To the extent they claim to have been trying to improve the program, they failed miserably and should feel bad about their efforts.

Overall a devaluation, but not a large one. Neither of the key improvements I’ve repeatedly suggested happened (make club awards useable for breakfast at hotels without a club, make cat 1-4 night awards cat 1-5 or 1-6 so they covered most “normal” hotels as they used to).

losing globalist free parking on award stays is a sizable loss. for 2026 qualified globalists, hyatt should add 1-4 free parking awards in 2027 to soften thid unexpected blow. cc spending globalists will feel the brunt. many will rethink and some change 2027 cc spending habits.

I’ve got a reservation using points for NYE + 2 nights. So, am I going to get screwed on the free parking? Of course, this is the first time having to park a car on a points stay in a long time.

They badly need the option to top up cat 1-4 certs with points like Marriott has. The desirable properties keep getting moved to cat 5.

I have a problem with taking away free parking. Do we know if the new rules are taking effect January 1, 2027 for those earning Globalist for 2027? We would not have had the option to get a free parking pass as yet.

Hi Gary, Great review! Any change to the number and type of awards given to lifetime globalist?

Once again, the shorter expiration date on the suite upgrade awards may cause some to delay achieving a milestone so they could have one to use in December, January, or February. Hopefully they still keep the 90 day period to choose.

I like the changes and excellent analysis, Gary-very fair reading!

Now, I want to know when the premium Hyatt card will be launched and what mechanisms it will have to shorten one’s way towards Globalist.

Along those lines, will Hyatt permit holders of this card to top off any and or all certificates? Marriott has permittied this, IHG has permitted this and it is time that Hyatt does as well, seeing that Chase issues cards for all 3 chains.

Moreover, it will be in the spirit of permitting a milestone award seeker a more tailored award.

I may not value many Category 7 properties, but perhaps a Category 5 or 6 speaks more to me — if given a choice between 2 Category 4 awards that can be topped off as opposed to 1 Category 7 award, the choice would be easy.

Gary, I have until Jan 21 to make my choice for 50 nights. I used to wait until January to get the longer expiration date (Feb 2029 instead of Feb 2028).

Does this impact choices already earned in other words if I wait until January to choose I will get a shorter expiration date that if I for the suite upgrade awards then if I chose in December?

Anyone know if you earn a milestone in 2026 but select it in 2027 if it will have a Feb 2029 expiration? You have 90 days to choose I can’t imagine two different expiration dates based on when issued but maybe?

My reaction: Cat 1-4 awards remain close to useless. Fix that and we can talk.

Loss of parking sucks. We drive to the Hyatt Regency Huntington Beach resort and parking is $60 a night. Kids grew up at the resort. My concierge has been super helpful. Booking the suite at Grand Hyatt Tokyo you can’t select 4 people to book a standard room but a suite can sleep 4 so I had to call into the concierge to explain the issue since I couldn’t book online and she was able to book us with points apply the SUA and change to 4 person occupancy. Maybe I can do that without a concierge but it sure helps to have someone on the phone doing that for me. Love the upgrade on free night certificates.

@nsx at FlyerTalk — For. Real. Dawg. For. Real.

@principal lewis – LALF stated that Globalist status earned in 2026 included free parking until Feb 2028 so, based on that, they plan to honor it next year. IMHO, a borderline change. Sure I used it a few times if I traveled and rented a car but much of my travel is international w no car. Also, someone complained about it being removed for road warriors who stayed 60 plus nights – well I suspect you are traveling on OPM and can expense the parking so, again, no big loss.

The loss of parking will directly impact me. I think I’ve probably used that on 6 nights this year, including valet at PH Auckland and Seabird. And while I never email my concierge, I do frequently call the concierge number and greatly value the fast, competent service.

The 365 day expiration for a SUA is horrible. No longer possible to confirm a SUA before registration opens. And if trying to secure a suite a year in advance, you have to time when you earn the reward. This is an incentive to stay elsewhere so you don’t hit the milestone too early and have to select an award before you want it.

Also, can premium suite discount be used on a cash + points booking?
